deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 8-10): Grothendieck axiomatizes small categories M of 'standard shapes' such as the simplex category with injective maps, a rigidified cube category, and the globe ('hemisphere') category. For each object n he takes I_n, the poset of facets (subobjects) of n. I_n has a greatest element d_n and a strictly increasing dimension map τ_n: I_n → N̄. For each facet ξ of dimension n' there is a distinguished 'standard' map u^n_ξ: I_{n'} → I_n. It is an isomorphism onto the down-set (I_n)_{≤ξ} and sends d_{n'} to ξ. These maps compose by the rule u^n_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η = u^n_ζ, where ζ = u^n_ξ(η).

This page finishes the construction begun on p. 8:
- M_0 has object set N̄. Its Hom(n',n) is the set of admissible maps I_{n'} → I_n, i.e. the u^n_ξ, which are closed immersions (down-set embeddings). Composition is ordinary composition of maps, closed by the rule above.
- There is a canonical, choice-free functor M → M_0, sending an object to its index and a morphism to its induced map on facet posets.
- This functor is an equivalence. It is an isomorphism exactly when M is reduced (skeletal).
- Assuming M reduced, M is identified with M_0. M_0 is therefore wholly determined by combinatorial data:
  - an ordered set N̄;
  - posets I_n, each with a top element d_n;
  - strictly increasing maps τ_n with image N̄_{≤n} and τ_n^{-1}(n) = {d_n};
  - injections ρ_{n,n'}: τ_n^{-1}(n') → Hom(I_{n'}, I_n), ξ ↦ u^n_ξ, satisfying the down-set isomorphism and composition axioms.

The next page states the converse: such data define a category satisfying (i) and (ii). It then lists the examples (simplices; 'épinglé' cubes; hemispheres D_n with 2n+1 facets) and the topological condition that |J_n minus d_n| is an (n−1)-sphere and |J_n| an n-disk.

In modern terms this is a combinatorial presentation of a skeletal direct (Reedy-type) category. In it all maps are monic, every slice M/n is a poset, there are no non-identity automorphisms, and Hom(n',n) is in bijection with the n'-dimensional facets of n. The aim is apparently to describe the 'shape categories' used to model cells, in the spirit of Pursuing Stacks (test categories, hemispherical/globular complexes).
errors: The composition axiom as written in the transcription (u^{n'}_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η) is index-inconsistent. It must be u^n_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η = u^n_ζ, as on the previous page.

Implicit assumption: Hom_M(n',n) bijects with τ_n^{-1}(n'), i.e. every morphism is monic and rigid with no non-trivial automorphisms. Otherwise M → M_0 is not faithful and so not an equivalence. This is presumably conditions (i)/(ii) stated earlier; the cube example needs the 'épinglage' precisely to kill the symmetries.

Minor: the transcription has ℕ where the page has an ordered set N̄ (the next page notes N̄ = N in the examples). The axiom τ_n(I_n) = N̄_{≤n} presupposes the set of realized dimensions below n is all of N̄_{≤n}.

ideas.what: Encoding a rigid category of cell shapes by facet posets I_n with dimension functions and standard down-set embeddings satisfying a cocycle-type composition rule. This reconstructs the category up to isomorphism (equivalence in general).
ideas.modern_name: Skeletal direct category with poset slices / regular (elegant) Reedy category of cells; face-poset presentation of a regular cell category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Reedy categories: Reedy (1974), Kan; elegant/regular Reedy categories: Bergner–Rezk (2013); regular CW posets: Björner (1984)
ideas.where_published: Related material on test categories and globes/hemispheres is in Pursuing Stacks (1983); this exact axiomatization, unsure

ideas.what: Canonical functor M → M_0 is an equivalence, and an isomorphism iff M is skeletal ('réduite').
ideas.modern_name: Skeleton of a category; recovering a category from its subobject posets

ideas.what: Examples and topological condition from the neighbouring page: facets of n realize to an n-disk with boundary an (n−1)-sphere. Examples are simplices, 'épinglé' cubes (ordered pairs of opposite faces with a chosen + face) and globes D_n with 2n+1 facets.
ideas.modern_name: Regular CW-ball face posets; globular/cubical/simplicial site; 'hemispherical' (globular) sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (regular CW posets); globular sets: Street, Batanin; Grothendieck in Pursuing Stacks

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives an intrinsic combinatorial axiomatization of 'categories of cell shapes' via facet posets, rank functions and standard down-set embeddings. Combined with the next page's sphere/disk condition, this amounts to 'rigid regular-CW cell categories'. It anticipates later abstract frameworks: regular/elegant Reedy categories, regular cell complexes as presheaves, and Henry's/Campion's axiomatics of shape categories. He links it explicitly to the simplicial, rigidified cubical and globular cases.
missed.quote: peut-on l'identifier à la catégorie M_0, définie par les données N̄, (I_n), (τ_n : I_n → N̄), (ρ_{n,n'}) ... satisfaisant u^n_ξ : I_{n'} ≅ (I_n)_{≤ξ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck (likely around Pursuing Stacks) treating shape categories uniformly via face posets with a regular-CW condition, a viewpoint later rediscovered independently. Little new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but fairly routine reconstruction of a rigid direct category from its facet posets. Interest lies in the early uniform axiomatization of shape categories (simplices, épinglé cubes, globes) tied to a regular-CW condition. Similar notions exist in the later literature, so no genuinely new result is present.
transcription_corrections: The base ordered set is written N̄ (barred N), not ℕ; τ_n(I_n) = N̄_{≤n}.
Line 1 likely reads 'la composition des hom. admiss. étant celle des hom (entre les I_n)'. The inserted word under 'composition' looks like 'admiss.', not 'identités'.
'(indépendant de tout choix, ... , évident)': the middle words are uncertain, possibly 'il n'y en a pas'. The struck '(défini' is correct.
'c'est un isom. de catégories ssi M est une catégorie réduite': 'ssi' rather than 'si'.
'Je vais supposer par la suite M réduite. On peut donc l'identifier à la catégorie M_0', rather than '— peut-on l'identifier'.
Composition axiom: u^n_ξ ∘ u^{n'}_η = u^n_ζ with ζ = u^n_ξ(η), for ξ ∈ I_n, η ∈ I_{n'}, n' = τ_n(ξ), n'' = τ_{n'}(η).
τ_n^{-1}(n) = {d_n} (plus grand élément); Hom_{M_0}(n',n) indexed by (n',n) with n' ≤ n.
